h1: The best progress photo apps in 2026, compared
dek: The scale can't tell fat from water or muscle. Photos can, if every one is taken the same way. We compared how Fimbl, Progress, Hevy, MacroFactor, MyFitnessPal and Cronometer help you capture, compare and protect your body transformation photos.

faq.q: What is the best app for progress photos?
faq.a: It depends on what else you track. For progress photos alongside a food diary and weight, Fimbl offers guided front, side, back and face photos, live on-device alignment, auto-capture, side-by-side and swipe compare and a time-lapse, all free and stored only on your iPhone. Progress is a strong dedicated photo app with a passcode lock and iCloud sync, and Hevy suits people who already log workouts.

faq.q: How do I take consistent progress photos?
faq.a: Use the same spot, light, time of day, clothing, camera height and distance every time, and the same poses: front and side at minimum, back if you can. Prop the phone up and use a timer rather than a mirror. An app with an overlay of your last photo, or Fimbl's live alignment guide, makes lining up much easier.

faq.q: How often should I take progress photos?
faq.a: Every one to two weeks is plenty. Daily photos mostly show day-to-day noise such as water and food, and frequent body checking can increase body dissatisfaction for some people. Taking photos together with a weigh-in keeps the rhythm simple.

faq.q: Why do I look different but weigh the same?
faq.a: The scale combines fat, muscle, water and glycogen. Weight naturally rises and falls through the week, and if you're training while eating less you can gain muscle while losing fat. In one trial, people gained 1.2 kg of lean mass while losing 4.8 kg of fat in four weeks, so the scale understated the change. Photos capture shape changes the scale misses.

faq.q: Are progress photos in fitness apps private?
faq.a: It varies. Many apps upload photos to the company's servers or cloud. Others, such as Fimbl, keep them on your phone. In Fimbl, progress photos are never uploaded, never used for AI, encrypted on the device and excluded from iCloud backups. The trade-off is that they don't transfer to a new phone unless you save copies to Photos.

faq.q: Can an app measure body fat from a photo?
faq.a: Some apps estimate it, usually by sending your photos or video to a server for analysis. The estimates are rough: an independent study of two smartphone apps found typical errors of 3.9 to 6.2 percentage points compared with a laboratory method. Consistent photos and a weight trend are more useful for tracking your own change.
